correctness.rationale: Mostovoy 2026 Theorem 1 supplies rational homology concentration and ranks. For an orthogonal reflection every fixed finite subset has a unique equatorial/paired-hemisphere decomposition, yielding (1+z)^{chi(S^{d-1})}(1+z^2)^{chi_c(R^d)} exactly via compact-support configuration Euler identities. The explicit coefficient sums give the fixed Euler characteristics. Equivariant triangulation ensures Lefschetz equals this Euler characteristic; in odd dimensions one unknown sign is uniquely solved. In even dimensions top oriented configuration strata carry det^n because excluded diagonals have codimension d>=2, and Lefschetz forces det^(n-1) in the other degree. The connected special orthogonal group acts homotopically trivially. For finite orthogonal G, rational quotient cochains identify with invariant cochains, whose invariants functor is exact; the stated quotient ranks follow. The standalone finite checker reproduced 2193 parameter cases and all predicted Burnside Euler identities; proof covers all indices.

value.rationale: Isometry actions and finite symmetry quotients are intrinsic to finite subsets of a sphere. The rational homology from the motivating 2026 paper alone loses all orientation character data. Determining the reflection sign and the resulting rational homology of all finite orthogonal quotients gives the explicit sharp odd-dimensional n modulo four acyclicity transition, with infinitely many quotient spaces on both sides. The result is a structural all-parameter classification, not a finite table or a restatement of ordinary homology ranks; it distinguishes rationally acyclic quotients from rational homology spheres without making unsupported contractibility claims.
